title: Cap. IX vocatione Sol cont.: reprobates may be commanded to believe and offered salvation if they believe — as non-elect angels were commanded to obey
pass_a_gloss: Now as to what pertains unto the reprobate, eternal antecedent reprobation notwithstanding, it can as well be commanded unto them that they believe, as it could truly be commanded unto the non-elect or reprobate Angels that they obey God: salvation can as well be offered unto them under the condition, If they believe, as beatitude could be promised unto those under the condition, If they had persevered in the obedience of God. For as the predestination of Peter does not take away the truth of this negative conditional, If thou shalt not have believed, thou shalt not be saved: so the reprobation of Judas does not enervate the truth of this affirmative conditional, If thou shalt have believed, thou shalt be saved: but infers only, that indissoluble conditional concatenation of faith and salvation standing, that efficacious grace is not to be given unto Judas by which he would in fact fulfill the condition.
pass_b_english: As for the reprobate: eternal antecedent reprobation notwithstanding, they can as truly be commanded to believe as the non-elect or reprobate angels could be commanded to obey God; salvation can as truly be offered them on the condition If they believe as beatitude could be promised those angels on If they had persevered in God's obedience. Peter's predestination does not cancel the truth of If you do not believe, you will not be saved; Judas's reprobation does not weaken If you believe, you will be saved. It only implies that, that indissoluble faith-salvation bond standing, Judas is not to be given the efficacious grace by which he would in fact fulfill the condition.
source_text: Jam quod attinet ad reprobatos, non obstante aeterna antecedanea reprobatione, tam potest iis mandari ut credant, quam potuit vere mandari Angelis non-electis sive reprobatis ut obediant Deo: tam potest iis offerri salus sub conditione, Si credant, quam potuit his promitti beatitudo sub conditione, Si in obsequio Dei perseverassent. Nam ut praedestinatio Petri non tollit veritatem hujus negativae conditionalis, Si non credideris, non salvaberis: ita reprobatio Judae non enervat veritatem hujus affirmativae conditionalis, Si tu credideris, tu salvaberis: sed infert solummodo, stante indissolubili illa conditionali fidei et salutis concatenatione, non dandam eam efficacem gratiam Judae, qua de facto conditionem impleat.
